features.feature: User-visible reviewer_list emits proof-or-stop-review-* canonical lanes.
A persisted lattice-review-* run is normalized to the matching canonical reviewer lane without changing historical evidence bytes.
New review_run_start, finding_add, review_pass_set, and init_check_set evidence writes use canonical proof-or-stop-* role IDs.

All 16 canonical role IDs, including the four formerly unprefixed roles, are represented in template filenames/frontmatter, prompt registry records, host shims, Codex manifests, and dispatch resolution.
agent_prompt resolves a canonical role body and gives a precise legacy-alias warning or replacement for old role IDs.
delivery_check_set plus delivery/floor consumers write and read canonical role IDs with legacy compatibility.
Process-fact registry and its contract verifier normalize canonical and legacy role IDs.
Codex, Claude Code, and Antigravity host resolution has golden coverage for the same canonical role IDs.
Legacy role alias sunset is machine-defined: terminal evidence remains readable, new legacy writes stop, and removal has a non-terminal-reference plus two-release condition.
A malformed or non-reviewer role cannot enter a reviewer lane merely by containing a canonical or legacy prefix.
New managed files and init --upgrade emit proof-or-stop:start/end markers.
Readers locate existing lattice:start/end blocks and replace them in place without duplication or orphaning.
Mismatched or nested managed markers are rejected or left unchanged rather than destructively rewritten.
Every in-scope new artifact writer uses proof-or-stop.* while preserving the schema suffix and version.
Artifact readers accept corresponding lattice.* schemas and retain existing integrity and freshness validation.
Unknown artifact prefix, suffix, or version is rejected and archived story JSON is never rewritten.
A complete schema/writer/reader/freshness matrix exists for every gate-consumed artifact and its process-fact/residue contract.
Two named archived stories from different eras are read and their historical signatures verify after the migration.
New release approvals use proof-or-stop.remote-push-approval.v1 and are accepted by the hook.
Old lattice.remote-push-approval.v1 remains readable during the window; stale or invalid approvals fail closed and a valid approval is consumed only once.
Root package.json and root lockfile identity entries become proof-or-stop with synchronized versions.
proof-or-stop --version visibly reports Proof-or-Stop rather than a legacy product name.
Self-host detection accepts the canonical package identity without silently bypassing the safety gate.
@proof-or-stop/utils and @proof-or-stop/lab metadata, lockfiles, dependency edges, and imports form a resolvable package graph.
The global lab entrypoint resolves canonical sibling packages and no exact-name consumer leaves a mixed old/new graph.
The installed main package exposes proof-or-stop and omits the lattice bin alias.
Help, entrypoint, residue, and generated invocation checks reject unsupported lattice command aliases while preserving explicit compatibility readers.
The removed bin aliases are announced in CHANGELOG.md as required by the identity-migration decision.
